_meta.source: Salih 05: German v2 (Elias->Ilyas; 'Tälern'->'Ebenen' al-A'raf 7:74; 'Abmachung nicht einhalten' -> 'taten nichts Gutes' an-Naml 27:48; 'Salih war sehr traurig' removed; 'Schrei vom Himmel' -> 'Schrei' ; 'sagte traurig' -> 'wandte sich ab' 7:79; H55). Complete verse quoted: al-A'raf 7:79. Rest in Oma's words (Hud 11:61-68, ash-Shu'ara 26:141-158, al-A'raf 7:73-79, an-Naml 27:48, ash-Shams 91:12).

s01: Shhh… Noah, Ilyas… do you see this little camel?
s02: Once there was a she-camel that was quite different from all other camels. She was a sign from Allah.
s03: Tonight I will tell you her story: the story of the Prophet Salih, peace be upon him.
s04: After the people of ʿAd lived a people called Thamud. They were very skilful. They carved their houses into the rocks of the mountains, and in the plains they built beautiful palaces.
s05: Allah gave them gardens and springs, fields and date palms. But they forgot Allah, who had given them all this, and worshipped idols.
s06: So Allah sent them a man from their own people: the Prophet Salih.
s07: He said: O my people, worship Allah alone. He created you from the earth and let you live on it. So ask Him for forgiveness.
s08: But they said: O Salih, we had great hopes in you. And now you say such a thing?
s09: Then they demanded: Bring us a sign if you are telling the truth.
s10: And Allah sent them a wonderful sign: a she-camel. Salih said: This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you. Let her eat freely on Allah’s earth, and do not touch her with harm.
s11: And there was an agreement: one day the she-camel drinks from the water, and the next day you.
s12: Grandma, that is fair, isn’t it?
s14: But in the city there were nine men who only spread mischief, and they did nothing good.
s15: What do you think, did the others stop them? No. The worst of them stepped forward, and they did something very evil to the she-camel of Allah, until she died.
s16: And then they said rudely: O Salih, bring us the punishment you threaten us with.
s17: He said: Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three more days. That is a promise that is not a lie.
s18: One day passed, two days, three days. And then came a mighty cry, and the earth shook.
s19: And afterwards their houses were silent and empty, as if no one had ever lived there. But Allah saved the Prophet Salih and those who believed with him, by His mercy.
s20: Allah says about Salih: “And he turned away from them and said, ‘O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors.’”
s21: Noah? Ilyas? They are already asleep.
s22: Sleep well, my little stars, and remember: always be kind to animals, keep your promises, and listen to good advice.
s23: And tomorrow I will tell you about the Prophet Ibrahim and a fire that became cool. Good night.
